HAND-AUTHORED, NOT RECORDED. Read this before trusting these files.

No BRAINTRUST_API_KEY exists on the machine that created this package, so no
live exchange produced these files. They are hand-authored against the
documented Braintrust REST schema as of 2026-08-29 (the vendor's API docs at
https://www.braintrust.dev/docs/reference/api):

  - Dataset resolution: GET {host}/v1/dataset?dataset_name=<name>
    [&org_name=<org>]. This is a FILTER endpoint, not a lookup: an unknown
    name is answered 200 with an EMPTY array, never a 404. Each dataset
    object carries id (a uuid), name, project_id, created_at, metadata,
    deleted_at, version.
  - Dataset events:    GET {host}/v1/dataset/{dataset_id}/fetch?limit=100
    [&cursor=<opaque>] [&org_name=<org>], response envelope {events: [...],
    cursor: <opaque string>}. The fetch limit counts TRACES, not rows, so a
    response can legally exceed limit events — the row and page byte caps
    are the real bounds. An absent or empty cursor field is the last page.
    Each event carries id (a uuid), input (JSON, nullable), expected (JSON,
    nullable), metadata, tags, created_at, updated_at, _xact_id, and
    optionally origin. _xact_id is the version counter: the dataset object
    has NO updatedAt or revision field, so the fingerprint leans on the
    newest event's _xact_id instead.
  - Origin: an event whose row carries origin {object_type, object_id,
    _xact_id} was copied from another object ("expected output from a
    span..."). The object_type values recorded in these fixtures at
    hand-author time: "experiment", "span", "eval_result". They are NOT
    enumerated in the adapter: the PRESENCE of origin is the derived signal,
    whatever the object type, so a new object type needs no code change —
    but the fixtures are re-judged against live captures when they exist.
  - Auth: Authorization: Bearer <BRAINTRUST_API_KEY>, per Braintrust's API
    documentation.
  - Base URL: the vendor SDKs default to https://api.braintrust.dev and
    honor a BRAINTRUST_API_BASE_URL override; this adapter mirrors both.
    That claim is a documentation claim like the rest of this note, subject
    to the same re-record review.

The schemas are versioned and can change — that is the adapter's accepted
drift risk, recorded in docs/plans/2026-08-29-braintrust-evals-adapter.md.

Until a real exchange replaces them, the adapter rests on a documentation
claim rather than on evidence. When BRAINTRUST_API_KEY exists, re-record:

  make record-fixtures

(or directly: KNO_LIVE_TESTS=1 KNO_RECORD_FIXTURES=1 go test -tags=integration
  ./adapters/evals/braintrust/ -run TestRecordLiveFixtures)

which captures the live dataset list response and its first fetch page into
testdata/live/ (and refuses to record a response that echoes a key). Those
captures are the evidence to review against these files. The malformed,
empty, duplicate, null-input, and origin fixtures cannot be recorded — no
live dataset is malformed — so they stay hand-authored and are judged
against the captures.

What each fixture is for:

  dataset-list.json              name resolution; one dataset, id
                                 8f1c4b2e-5d6a-4f8e-9c2d-1a3b5c7d9e0f, name
                                 support-llm
  dataset-list-miss.json         the FILTER-endpoint miss: an EMPTY array
                                 (never a 404) -> "no dataset named" refusal
  dataset-list-two.json          two datasets with the same name -> the
                                 multi-match refusal
  dataset-list-wrong-name.json   one dataset with a different name -> the
                                 filter-ignored refusal
  events-page1.json              first fetch page (2 rows: an escape/unicode
                                 row and a nested-key-order row), cursor
                                 "cur-2"; _xact_ids 100 and 99
  events-page2.json              page 2 (a key-unsorted input whose canonical
                                 JSON the goldens pin, and a null expected ->
                                 empty Expected); last page (empty cursor);
                                 _xact_ids 98 and 97
  events-empty.json              a dataset that exists with no events ->
                                 zero Cases
  events-dup-page1.json          the merge rule, first half: ev-dup-0001 at
                                 _xact_id 200 (the newest version, served
                                 first by the newest-first walk) plus
                                 ev-dup-0002 at 199
  events-dup-page2.json          the merge rule, second half: ev-dup-0001
                                 AGAIN at _xact_id 150 — the same row's
                                 pre-edit version re-exposed by the version
                                 history, exactly the duplicate the vendor
                                 documents on later pages — plus
                                 ev-dup-0003 at 198. One ev-dup-0001 is
                                 yielded (the newest), never twice, never
                                 fatal (plan P0-2). An edit mid-pagination
                                 produces exactly this shape.
  events-null-input.json         an event whose input is null -> fatal
  events-origin.json             origin object_type values experiment, span,
                                 and eval_result -> Provenance.Derived with
                                 the object named; one authored row -> not
  events-null-expected.json      a null expected -> empty Expected, named
  golden/canonical.json          the pinned canonical-JSON encoding: key
                                 order, HTML escaping, and unicode behavior
